en.title: First Team's Wins over Same-Index Pairs (Another Source)
en.description:
Each of two teams has n people. For each same-index pair i<j, the first team wins if the skill sum of its two people is strictly greater than that of the corresponding two people on the second team; a tie is not a win. Count the wins modulo 1000000007. The index typesetting on this page is missing; the corresponding-index rule is restored from the full statement and identical examples of amazon-group1-win-count.md in the same snapshot.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line the first team's skills, and the third line the second team's skills. 2≤n≤100000; all skills are in 1..10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 1, 0 and 3. You cannot sort the two teams separately and then subtract.
hints: First compute the skill difference between the two teams at each original index, then sort the differences and use two pointers to count unordered index pairs whose sum is strictly greater than 0.
